headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an overall effect size of 1.17 (95% CI: 1.06–1.29), suggesting that ultra-processed food intake is associated with a higher risk of kidney and renal pelvis cancer. These findings were supported by low between-study heterogeneity (I² = 0.00%), indicating consistent findings across the included studies.
